items.note: AEA registry entry for an RCT in which engineering student venture teams get training in generative-AI use for early-stage business ideas versus traditional creativity-tool training, with external judges grading problem relevance and value proposition (innovation component); registration only, no results found, randomization is at the group level (at least 130 groups per the registry, not in the abstract), and novelty is not an explicit outcome.

Difference-in-differences natural experiment on 1.5 million Change.org petitions around the rollout of an in-platform write-with-AI tool, plus repeat writers before and after; AI access raised petition homogeneity without improving outcomes; it compares real output across time and access, with no assigned participants (journal version in Nature Human Behaviour, same study as arXiv 2511.13949); classified from the arXiv abstract because OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned none for the DOI.

Controlled experiment with 123 product innovators in three conditions (no AI, moderate AI assistance, high AI assistance), scoring the number, originality, and feasibility of ideas; inverted-U result; the abstract does not say how participants were assigned.

Quasi-experiment with 97 third-graders, assigned at random by intact class to a GenAI chatbot (n = 48) or a search engine (n = 49) during inquiry learning, with problem-posing ability and problem quality scored; this is AI versus another aid, assignment is at the class level (likely two classes), and next stage should judge whether problem posing counts as a creativity outcome.

Preregistered online experiment (N = 554) and a museum naturalistic experiment (N = 36,198) in which trained AI models give real-time originality feedback on participants' ideas and sketches, raising rated originality; the AI evaluates rather than generates content, so the next stage must check whether the scoring models count as generative AI (possible not_generative_ai), and assignment in the museum study is not stated.

HCI system paper with a comparative user study of Creo, a multi-stage sketch-to-image system, against a one-shot text-to-image baseline (AI configuration versus AI configuration), with embedding analysis showing less homogeneous outputs; the sample size is not in the abstract (search notes say 15, within-subjects, counterbalanced) and the homogeneity measure may be within-session rather than across people.

Online experiment (n = 102) comparing people who generate ideas with AI support against people working alone, scored on Torrance dimensions: AI raised fluency, elaboration, and flexibility but lowered originality; ECIS 2024 conference paper, assignment not stated in the abstract.

Engineering (N = 99) and psychology (N = 212) students wrote a design solution, evaluated pre-generated GPT-3.5 ideas, and revised, with originality and effectiveness rated; the only AI contrast is within-person before versus after exposure, with no no-AI control and no randomized order, so it likely fails the source-of-variation criterion at full text.

Within-subject experiment with 40 university students on design-problem modules with and without ChatGPT-4o, with consensual assessment of the originality and usefulness of design sketches; below 50 participants, and the abstract does not say whether the order of conditions was randomized.

Two studies of children telling stories with a social robot driven by a GPT-3 model fine-tuned to behave creatively or non-creatively (an AI configuration contrast): Study 1 (38 children, Wizard of Oz) found no effect, and Study 2 (103 children, autonomous robot) found higher fluency, flexibility, and elaboration; assignment method not stated in the abstract (search notes say balanced on pre-test creativity).
